definition: A resistor whose resistance can be changed, often with a sliding contact, to control the current in a circuit; with the supply p.d. unchanged, more resistance gives a smaller current.
A resistor whose resistance changes with temperature; for the NTC thermistor in this course, the resistance falls as the temperature rises.
A resistor (LDR) whose resistance changes with light: its resistance falls as the light falling on it gets brighter, and is high in the dark.
A switch worked by an electromagnet: a small current in the relay's coil magnetises it, and the coil closes (or opens) a switch in a second circuit that can carry a large current.
A safety device with a thin wire that melts when the current rises above the fuse's rating, breaking the circuit before the wires overheat.
Resistors (or a resistor with a sliding contact) in series across a supply, which share the supply p.d. so that a smaller p.d. can be taken from part of it.
A diode (LED) that gives out light when a current passes through it in the forward direction; in reverse almost no current flows and it stays dark.
